depth.transferChallenge: Change exactly one boundary in the sample — value, &T, or &mut T. Before compiling, list which bindings remain usable after each call. Keep the focus on add, display, from, and into.

answers: Into is derived alongside From automatically
A blanket impl gives Into to everything that implements From
The compiler special-cases .into() for every type
writing.exampleCaption: Implement From and Into arrives automatically.
writing.explanation: a + b calls Add::add, {} calls Display::fmt, and .into() calls Into, which you get for free by implementing From. Because they are normal traits, your own types participate in the same syntax as the built-in ones, and the compiler checks the result type at every use.
writing.feedback: The standard library has impl<T, U: From<T>> Into<U> for T.
writing.question: Why does .into() work without writing an Into impl?
